title: The Lord and the Seraphim
summary: In the year king Uzziah died, Nephi saw the Lord seated upon a high throne, with the Lord’s train filling the temple. Above it stood seraphim, each with six wings: two covering the face, two covering the feet, and two used to fly.

explicit_facts.text: In the year king Uzziah died, the first-person narrator saw the Lord sitting upon a high throne, and the Lord’s train filled the temple.
Seraphim stood above it. Each had six wings: two covered the face, two covered the feet, and two were used to fly.

unspecified_visual_details: The referent of “it” in “Above it stood the seraphim” is not explicit.
The Lord’s facial features and other physical characteristics are unspecified.
The number of seraphim is unspecified.
The temple’s architecture, throne design, colors, and lighting are unspecified.
Nephi’s appearance and viewing position are unspecified.

narration.text: In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
Above it stood the seraphim; each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supplied instruction identifies Nephi as the first-person narrator; the quoted verses do not name him.
King Uzziah’s death establishes the year and is not depicted as a separate event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict king Uzziah’s death or place him in the temple.
Do not invent dialogue or additional events.
Do not assign undescribed features to the Lord or seraphim as source-established facts.
Do not specify Nephi’s viewing position or treat the referent of “it” as certain.

title: The Cry and the Smoke
summary: One cries to another. The posts of the door move at the voice of the one who cried, and the house fills with smoke.

explicit_facts.text: One cried to another and spoke of the Lord of Hosts and his glory.
The posts of the door moved at the voice of the one who cried.
The house was filled with smoke.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Smoke can be shown inside the house.
The doorposts can be shown moving as the voice is heard.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of the two figures are unspecified.
The house’s design and the smoke’s appearance are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: One who cried

narration.text: And one cried unto another, and said:
And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statement about the whole earth is spoken dialogue, not a separately narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify either figure as a seraph or give either an invented appearance.
Do not identify the house as a temple.
Do not depict the Lord of Hosts or a visible manifestation of glory.

title: A Lament
summary: Nephi laments that he is undone, says he dwells among a people of unclean lips, and says he has seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi says he is undone and is a man of unclean lips.
Nephi says he dwells among a people of unclean lips.
Nephi says his eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.

unspecified_visual_details: Nephi's appearance, clothing, posture, and surroundings are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Wo is unto me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips; and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips; for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of Hosts.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supplied instruction identifies the first-person narrator as Nephi; the verse does not name Isaiah.
Nephi reports having seen the King; the verse does not place that sight during his speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the mentioned people or the King as visibly present.
Do not stage the reported sight of the King as a new event.
Do not depict unclean lips as visible contamination.
Do not invent a location, additional events, or dialogue.

title: The Live Coal
summary: One of the seraphim flies to Nephi carrying a live coal he had taken from the altar with tongs. He lays it upon Nephi’s mouth and speaks.

explicit_facts.text: One of the seraphim flew to Nephi with a live coal in his hand.
The seraph had taken the coal from the altar with tongs.
The seraph laid the coal upon Nephi’s mouth.
The seraph said the coal had touched Nephi’s lips, his iniquity was taken away, and his sin purged.

unspecified_visual_details: The encounter’s location and the altar’s position are unspecified.
The seraph’s appearance beyond his stated hand and flight is unspecified.
Nephi’s appearance and the designs of the altar and tongs are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Lo, this has touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Seraph

narration.text: Then flew one of the seraphim unto me, having a live coal in his hand,
And he laid it upon my mouth, and said:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi is identified as the first-person narrator by the user, not by name in these verses.
The removal of iniquity and purging of sin are the seraph’s declarations, not described visible transformations.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a temple setting or a spatial relationship to the altar.
Do not stage the earlier taking of the coal as a simultaneous action.
Do not import appearance details from unsupplied verses.
Do not invent additional figures, dialogue, burns, wounds, pain reactions, or visible purification effects.

title: Nephi Answers
summary: Nephi hears the Lord’s voice ask whom to send and who will go for them. Nephi offers to be sent.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi hears the voice of the Lord.
The Lord asks whom to send and who will go for them.
Nephi offers to be sent.

unspecified_visual_details: The Lord’s visible appearance is not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes the Lord’s voice, not a visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add a setting or a visible form for the Lord.

title: A Message to This People
summary: An unidentified speaker tells an addressee to deliver a message to this people, then speaks about their hearts, ears, eyes, conversion, and healing.

explicit_facts.text: A speaker tells an addressee to deliver a message to this people.
The speaker says the people did not understand or perceive.
The speaker gives instructions concerning the people's hearts, ears, and eyes, and mentions conversion and healing.

unspecified_visual_details: The verses specify no location or physical appearances.
The verses do not say that this people are present.

spoken_dialogue.text: Go and tell this people—Hear ye indeed, but they understood not; and see ye indeed, but they perceived not.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: Make the heart of this people fat, and make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes—lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted and be healed.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Place the narration before the spoken dialogue.
Nephi is the chapter's narrator, but these verses do not identify the speaker or addressee. The requested label “The Lord” is unsupported by the supplied verses.
The language about hearts, ears, and eyes is spoken instruction, not a narrated physical change.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the speaker as the Lord or the addressee as Nephi.
Do not invent appearances or a location.
Do not depict physical changes, conversion, or healing as occurring.
Do not depict this people as present in the exchange.

title: How Long?
summary: Nephi asks how long. A reply describes future desolation, the removal of men far away, and a great forsaking.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi addresses the Lord and asks how long.
A reply describes cities without inhabitants, houses without people, and a desolate land.
The reply describes the Lord removing men far away and a great forsaking in the land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown speaking and listening.
The question's address to the Lord supports identifying him as the respondent, though the reply introduces him only as “he.”
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and Nephi's appearance are unspecified.
No visible appearance of the Lord is described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: And the Lord have removed men far away, for there shall be a great forsaking in the midst of the land.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supplied instruction identifies the first-person narrator as Nephi.
The desolation, removal, and forsaking are described in the reply, not narrated as occurring during the exchange.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the predicted desolation, removal, or forsaking as present action.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord.
Do not add dialogue, characters, motives, or a specific setting.

title: The Holy Seed
summary: A tenth is foretold to return and be eaten. The verse compares this to a teil-tree and an oak, then calls the holy seed the substance thereof.

explicit_facts.text: A tenth is foretold to return and be eaten.
The verse compares this to a teil-tree and an oak whose substance is in them when they cast their leaves.
The holy seed is called the substance thereof.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the appearance of the tenth and the holy seed are not specified.

narration.text: But yet there shall be a tenth, and they shall return,
and shall be eaten, as a teil-tree, and as an oak whose substance is in them when they cast their leaves; so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trees are a comparison, not a narrated visible event. The return and being eaten are foretold, not shown happening.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign the verse to a speaker not identified by the supplied text.
Do not stage the foretold events or depict the comparison as a literal event.
